verdict.rationale: Riveter's own marketing describes scheduled projects that monitor for changes, refresh as often as every minute, and track competitor pricing, so recurring change monitoring is a first-party capability. Notification is only documented as run-completion webhooks (run.completed/stopped/finished) that POST full results, not alerts that fire when content actually changes. missing for 10: change-detection/diff semantics, change-triggered notifications rather than per-run completion webhooks, technical docs for scheduling or monitoring configuration, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a data-engineer, I can monitor target pages for content changes, such as price or listing updates, and get notified as they happen

citations.quote: Schedule any project to monitor for changes and keep your data fresh.
For fast moving data like scores or election results, you can refresh as often as every minute.
Automatically track competitor pricing, features, positioning, vendors, and payment providers.
Pass webhook_url in the JSON body when starting a run and Riveter POSTs the full results to your URL when it finishes (events: run.completed, run.stopped, run.finished).
